# Instructor guide · Topic 11: Searching

<!-- generated by tools/export-docs.mjs from topics/ and questions/: do not edit by hand -->

## Learning objectives

Know when a linear scan is enough, write binary search without off-by-one bugs, and recognise its variations: first/last position, insert position, rotated arrays and searching on the answer.

By the end of the topic, students can:

- **Linear search:** Check each element in turn.
- **Binary search:** On sorted data, look at the middle: it tells you which half cannot contain the target.
- **Boundaries: first, last and insert position:** Many questions are not “is it there?” but “where does it start?” or “where would it go?”.
- **Binary search on the answer:** If “does value x work?” is No, No, …, No, Yes, Yes, …, binary search can find the first Yes, even when there is no array at all.
- **Rotated and 2D searches:** Binary search still works when the data is only “partly” sorted, as long as each step can rule out half.

## Duration and prerequisites

- Lessons: about **47 minutes** of guided material (5 lessons)
- Practice: 15 coding problems and 26 quick questions in the bank; plan at least as much practice time as lesson time
- Suggested format: one 90-minute session
- Prerequisites: Topic 4 (Arrays / Python Lists)

Open the topic in the browser (`#t/searching`) and project it; every lesson alternates a short explanation with questions the class answers together.

## Live coding demonstrations

- Code the first “Code it” problem of each lesson live, thinking aloud.
- Brute force → optimal walkthrough: **Koko Eating Bananas: try every speed → binary search on the answer** (Challenge tab). Code the brute force, ask students to find the repeated work, then refactor.
- Visualizers to drive while students predict the next step: Linear search · Binary search

## Questions to ask the class

Ask, wait for several answers, then reveal (the answers are on the topic's Review flashcards).

- Binary search requirement?
- Inclusive bounds loop?
- Half-open [low, high) loop?
- First occurrence?
- bisect_left?
- Search on the answer?
- Rotated array?

## Classroom exercises (individual, 10–15 minutes each)

- Linear Search (`bs-linear`)
- Binary Search (`bs-search`)
- Search Insert Position (`bs-insert`)

Code tracing on the board: bisect_left vs bisect_right (`bs-p1`), The middle index (`bs-p2`), Count the steps (`bs-p3`), Insert position (`bs-p4`)

Find-the-bug warm-ups: The last element is never checked (`bs-d1`), Not the FIRST occurrence (`bs-d3`)

## Pair programming (25–30 minutes)

One driver types, one navigator thinks ahead and checks edge cases; swap every 10 minutes.

- First and Last Position (`bs-first-last`)
- Search in Rotated Sorted Array (`bs-rotated`)

## Homework

- Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array (`bs-rotated-min`)
- Find a Peak Element (`bs-peak`)
- Median of Two Sorted Arrays (`bs-median-two`)
- Finish the topic's Review quiz in the browser and clear the revision queue.

- Reference solutions: `solutions/11_searching/` (also behind “Show solution” in the browser).
